tours.title: How Vite serves development and builds production output
tours.summary: Vite is a web build tool with a development server and a production build command. The server serves modules to a browser and watches files as developers work. The builder prepares deployable output through configured environments. This tour follows those two paths from the command line.

steps.note:
### Vite gives development and production separate paths

The development server responds to browser requests and watches project files. The production builder prepares output for deployment.

code.find: It consists of two major parts:

steps.note:
### The command selects the work to start

The default command creates a development server. The build command creates a builder and runs its application build.

### Both paths resolve project settings

Configuration supplies the settings shared by both paths. The selected command decides which settings and plugins apply.

### Development builds a server, a hot-update channel and a file watcher

The dev server is an HTTP server around connect middlewares, a WebSocket server for hot updates, and a file watcher. The CLI then starts it with `server.listen`.

### Production runs the configured builder

The build command calls `buildApp`. The builder runs its configured application build; when that builds no environment, it builds every environment.

### Where to go next

The guide "How Vite chooses a hot update, reload, or no update" follows one file change to its outcome. This tour did not open the transform middleware, which answers each module request from the browser.
